A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRIFT-Net research. All 14 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Methods, equations, tables, and figures can be reliably matched despite substantial experimental additions.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original benchmark evaluations, rollout analyses, component ablations, and efficiency measurements on four Navier-Stokes tasks and two ApeBench Kolmogorov-flow variants.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations on three other PDE tasks, additional baselines and ablations, and the capacity, optimization, sample-efficiency, and resolution studies in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The architecture, low-frequency mixing, radial gating, frequency-weighted loss, spectral pipeline, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix F supplies configurations and task-specific input details without introducing a new DRIFT component or revising the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the four Navier-Stokes tasks and two ApeBench flow variants, while adding Poisson-Gauss, Allen-Cahn, and Wave-Gauss evaluations. This substantially broadens coverage to stationary elliptic, reaction-diffusion, and wave-propagation problems (Section 5, Table 1).

E2.justification: Table 1 adds U-NO, U-Net-ConvNeXt, and a Refiner U-Net adapted from PDE-Refiner alongside scOT and FNO, including comparisons on all four retained Navier-Stokes tasks. Refiner U-Net has no reported Poisson-Gauss result. The ApeBench comparisons remain against scOT.

E3.justification: v1 states approximately 20,000 trajectories and 40 epochs; v2 specifies task-dependent budgets, including 39,640 training trajectories and 20 epochs for NS-SL (Appendix F). This revises the reported settings without establishing that retained results were rerun. New experiments vary width, learning rate, schedule, sample count, and resolution, and introduce instantaneous error growth and training memory/time measurements.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds separate ablations of the depth-wise convolution and pointwise linear layer. Appendix G adds capacity, optimization sensitivity, sample-efficiency, cross-resolution, and computational-scaling analyses. Figure 3 replaces the NS-Tracer-PwC rollout-error analysis with instantaneous error growth on smoother ApeBench Kolmogorov flow. Existing spectral ablations and the qualitative visualization are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F.4 newly states that random seeds are fixed for each run. Neither version supplies seed values, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or variability estimates. This is a limited addition of seed information, not evidence of increased replication.

E6.justification: Shared headline error values and base-model throughput values are retained. New Table 1 results include DRIFT-Net/scOT errors of 0.86/0.87 on Poisson-Gauss, 1.03/1.10 on Allen-Cahn, and 12.15/12.34 on Wave-Gauss. Additional comparator, ablation, resource, and Appendix G results substantially expand the findings. The NS-Tracer rollout means and growth slopes reported in v1 are removed.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, method equations, Lipschitz and cumulative bounds, gating lemma, Sobolev defect theorem, and accompanying reasoning remain unchanged. Appendix F's added benchmark equations document experimental dynamics rather than introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central architectural contribution and headline claims of 7%-54% lower Navier-Stokes error and approximately 15% fewer parameters remain. The conclusion adds an explicit claim that accuracy benefits extend to elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic PDEs and describes DRIFT-Net as an integral-kernel backbone.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning image-branch importance, optimization robustness, approximate mesh independence under the tested interpolation setup, and manageable resolution scaling. The abstract softens the locality-to-drift statement from causation to association; substantive limitations remain unchanged. The new characterization of scOT as typically strongest is misleading: Table 1 contains stronger baselines on every Navier-Stokes task.

D1.justification: New Appendix F substantially expands reproducibility information: dataset shapes and splits, physical simulation parameters, model configurations and implementation links, from-scratch training, AdamW settings, batch size, checkpoint selection, and H200/FP32 hardware details. These are largely newly documented details; the main DRIFT-Net code-access statement is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 is reframed around a neural-operator taxonomy and explicitly positions DRIFT-Net within integral-kernel operators. It adds a survey, localized-kernel research, and discussion of MPP, DPOT, ICON, and CoDA-NO. The AFNO and Subramanian et al. references are removed, substantially changing the surrounding research context.

P1.justification: Related work and the conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 5 reorganizes baseline descriptions, main results, long-horizon analyses, and efficiency discussion, removing the redundant additional-final-time subsection. New structured setup and supplementary-experiment appendices expand the document organization, alongside terminology cleanup and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains task rows and comparator columns; Tables 3 and 4 expand; six new appendix tables appear. ApeBench rows move from Table 1 into a dedicated Table 2, replacing the earlier duplicate-results table. Figure 3 changes its dataset, quantity, axes, and caption. Other figures are retained or relocated, including Figure 5 from Appendix F to H.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical validation and sparse reproducibility documentation. Broader PDE coverage, additional competing architectures, targeted ablations, and controlled sensitivity studies make the retained method's strengths and applicability more assessable; Appendix F supplies important missing experimental details. These gains outweigh the loss of NS-Tracer rollout diagnostics and reporting weaknesses, including absent repeated-run uncertainty, unexplained budget revisions, and misleading baseline-ranking prose.
